name: 2.7 Measures of the Spread of the Data
_note: Complete on disk -- 12 questions. Seven were written 2026-08-09 and two more reused to finish the section. The standard deviation question separates the three stages so a wrong answer shows which stage lost it, and forces the mean onto a whole number by construction. The z-score question is built so the player with the HIGHER raw average has the LOWER z-score, which is the entire point of comparing across groups. The new ones cover the standard deviation from a frequency table (built as the xf and weighted squared-deviation columns), the two divisors on one squared total, what a standard deviation MEANS rather than how to compute it, converting between z-scores and raw values in both directions, the empirical rule turned into head counts rather than percentages, two samples with an identical range but very different spread, and which measures of spread survive an outlier -- the IQR is unchanged by construction there, as the median is in the 2.5 companion question.

questions.title: Standard Deviation Step by Step - Work a sample standard deviation through its three stages, the mean, the sum of squared deviations and the divide by n minus 1, then say what the finished number measures

Compare Across Groups with z-Scores - Convert two players' raw stats from different teams into z-scores to see who did better relative to his own team, then find a value a set number of standard deviations from a team mean

Five-Number Summary from an Unsorted Data Set - Sort a set of readings recorded out of order, find the two quartiles and the median, and compute the interquartile range that spans the middle half of the data
Same Range, Different Spread - Two data sets share a minimum and a maximum but not their standard deviations; compute the range of each, decide which is more spread out, and say what the range misses

Say What a Standard Deviation Means in Context - Give the units of a standard deviation, judge whether a stated value is unusually far from the mean, and pick the sentence that interprets the spread correctly
Standard Deviation from a Frequency Table - Build the xf and squared-deviation columns a grouped calculation needs, total them, and finish with the sample standard deviation
Sample Versus Population Standard Deviation - Compute both divisors on the same squared-deviation total, see which is larger, and say why a sample divides by one less
Which Measures of Spread Survive an Outlier - Find the range and the interquartile range, add one extreme value, recompute both, and identify which measures of spread are resistant
Find the Value a Given Number of Standard Deviations from the Mean - Convert between a z-score and a raw value in both directions, and read what a negative z-score says about a measurement
Compute a z-Score and Compare Two Values - Compute z = (x - mu) / sigma for a given observation and use z-scores to compare values from two different distributions
Empirical Rule (68-95-99.7) - Apply the empirical rule to estimate the percentage of values within one, two and three standard deviations of the mean

Turn the Empirical Rule into Head Counts - Find the interval one standard deviation either side of the mean, convert the 68-95-99.7 percentages into numbers of individuals, and say what the rule requires before it may be used
